stage_a.note: The presentation communicates strong positive engagement with warm smiles and enthusiastic delivery.
Sustained engaged excitement is evident as they describe the problem and their solution.
Friendly and approachable orientation characterizes the presentation, with considerate smiles.

venture.description: Heel caps that increase surface area to prevent high heels from sinking into grass or getting stuck in cracks.
venture.note: The founders ask for $500,000 for a 10% stake in their business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founders introduce themselves and their product, explaining how it prevents high heels from sinking into grass or cracks.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert asks Becca if she is currently wearing the product.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Becca confirms that both founders are wearing the heel caps.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Lori asks if the product comes in clear to match different shoe colors.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Monica confirms they offer the product in clear, black, silver, and gold.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin receives a sample box from the founders.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert asks how much the product costs.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Monica explains that each pair retails for $10, and a box of three pairs costs $30.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert expresses surprise and interest at the retail price.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Lori asks which samples are the silver and gold ones.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Becca deflects the question to invite the investors to try the product firsthand.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Becca invites Lori to come up and try a pair of heels.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert asks why the gentlemen are excluded from trying the heels.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Becca invites the men to try the product as well.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert approaches the stage to try on the heels.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert puts on the heels and expresses his surprise.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin reacts with amusement as Robert walks in the heels.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Becca explains to Robert that one heel has the cap and the other does not.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Daymond points out the difference, and Robert agrees he feels a huge difference.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin jokes that wearing heels is not a good look for Robert.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark asks the founders about their professional background.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Monica explains that they met working at Goldman Sachs right out of college.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert asks what happened after their time at Goldman Sachs.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Monica notes they learned a lot there, especially the importance of knowing who to go to.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin challenges their valuation, asking them to justify the five million dollar valuation.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Becca provides their revenue figures, stating they did $1.1 million last year and are growing.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert asks how they achieved that revenue and where they are selling the product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Monica lists retail partners like Nordstrom and explains that it is a highly correlated wedding purchase.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin asks if they are generating any cash flow yet.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Becca admits they are not generating cash flow because they are breaking even.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin asks if they are paying themselves a salary.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Monica confirms they are paying themselves and have 65% gross profit margins.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark asks how much the founders have personally invested.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Becca states they invested $100,000 together when they started.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark asks how much outside funding they have raised.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Becca replies they have raised just under a million dollars.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark asks how they raised the outside funding.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Monica explains they raised it from friends and angels.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Lori asks how many partners are currently in the business.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Becca clarifies that she and Monica together own 80%.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert challenges them on their distribution strategy, asking who they are selling to directly.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Monica confirms they sell to venues and hotels.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert asks how they plan to expand their distribution network.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Becca admits they have a bandwidth issue because it is just the two of them and one employee.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Daymond asks what the full-time employee's role is.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Becca states that the employee is their operations and office manager.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark challenges their expenses, asking where the $650,000 in gross margins is going.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Monica explains they use third-party workers like graphic designers and web developers.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert asks what their net profit was.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Becca states their net profit was $30,000.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Daymond asks how much they paid themselves.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Becca replies they each took an $80,000 salary last year.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin acknowledges the $160,000 salary expense makes the numbers add up.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Lori expresses doubt that the product is a strong necessity since many women wear more stable shoes.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Monica counters that for the occasions when stilettos are worn, the product acts as insurance.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Lori states she does not see it as a big enough problem and exits.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark exits because he does not believe the business can reach the scale required to justify the valuation.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Becca responds to Mark's challenge, stating they are committed and believe they can scale significantly.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin exits, arguing that scaling to fifty million in sales would require heavy reinvestment.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert praises the product as a new category and offers five hundred thousand for twenty-five percent.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Lori makes a remark about there being only one person left.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Daymond asks Kevin what he is doing.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin re-enters and offers one hundred thousand for ten percent with a four hundred thousand dollar loan.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Monica rejects Kevin's offer and counters Robert, asking if he would accept twenty percent.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert asks why a five percent difference is meaningful to them.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Monica explains that it allows them to maintain a slight cumulative majority.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark acknowledges their reasoning regarding their eighty percent ownership.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert agrees to the founders' counter offer.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert asks for final confirmation of the deal.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Becca accepts Robert's revised offer.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert thanks the founders and they share hugs and goodbyes.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Daymond comments that the business is not worth more than a million dollars.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert jokes that Kevin is turning green with envy.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Kevin replies that he would have preferred the debt deal.

decisions.note: Lori does not think the product solves a big enough problem since many women wear more stable shoes.
Mark exits because he does not believe they can scale to the sales volume required to justify the valuation.
Kevin exits, arguing that scaling to fifty million in sales would require heavy reinvestment and lower net profit.
Robert praises the product as a new category and wants more equity to help them scale.

decisions.terms: I sell a lot of products to women
decisions.note: Kevin re-enters because he likes the product and sees potential in the celebration market.
Kevin thinks the business is only worth one million dollars and prefers a debt structure.
Monica rejects Kevin's offer and asks Robert if he would accept twenty percent.
Robert agrees to the founders' counter offer.

record.notes: The founders conduct a demonstration with the investors trying on the heel caps on grass.
